steps.title: Important
steps.body: Terminology helps you discuss WHAT writers do. But don't just name techniques - always explain their EFFECT.

steps.title: Don't overuse terminology
steps.body: A strong essay doesn't name every technique. Use terminology when it helps you explain HOW a writer creates effect.

steps.title: Top Tip
steps.body: AO2 specifically rewards "relevant subject terminology where appropriate" — the keyword is "appropriate." A Grade 9 response uses terminology surgically: name the technique, then immediately explain its effect. Never list terms. An essay that names three techniques with precise effect analysis will always outscore one that names ten techniques with no explanation.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What's the difference between a metaphor and a simile? | What is a soliloquy and why is it useful for playwrights? | What does dramatic irony mean?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Metaphor says something IS something else ("life's a walking shadow"). Simile compares using "like" or "as" ("solitary as an oyster"). Metaphors create stronger, more direct connections. | A soliloquy is a speech where a character alone on stage speaks their thoughts aloud. It reveals inner thoughts directly to the audience, creating intimacy and showing psychological state. | Dramatic irony is when the audience knows more than the characters. It creates tension, makes audience complicit, and highlights characters' mistakes or blindness.
